newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise amid sluggish activity.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise amid sluggish activity.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Monday amid sluggish activity.
Traders said trade was thin because of the closure of many Latin American markets but prices were firm.
"The market was very quiet but firm," said an analyst at a foreign bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/4 to 90-3/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was $0.10 higher at 126.05.
Another trader said the market was looking forward to Tuesday's sale of Treasury bills at which 250 million pesos of 91-, and $250 million of 182-day bills will be auctioned.

"There is demand for peso bonds," said the trader, predicting that would be the case at the auction of peso bills as well. Traders forecast a discount strike rate of 6.50 percent for the 91-day bills, compared with 6.40 percent at last month's auction of similarly dated bills.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.90 percent from 6.0 percent.
